Only the encountered ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off RoW other-than-natural-gas district/industrial heat market is qualified. Preserve all 188 original market supplier coefficients, source order and marginal uncertainty individually, without omission, aggregation or normalization. Positive source and reconstructed heat reference 1 MJ means factor +1: negative caller heat credits remain negative. There is no district consumer network, loss uplift, efficiency multiplier, co-output credit, avoided fuel or material credit. Complete native useful-heat services include their own efficiency, infrastructure, fuel, emissions, ash handling and allocation. Furnace/wood species/feedstock/capacity matches remain distinct where available. Native historical CH, national coal and ENTSO-E coal fleets proxy missing source locations; historical UCTE is used for absent oil-power locations, not an invented global oil fleet. Native geographic text/identity contradictions, vintage, efficiency, emissions and internal uncertainty remain limitations. Wood CHP 1 MWth substitutes source 6667 kW CHP and 2014 variants. LPG 50 kW condensing/modulating propane/butane heat substitutes industrial >100 kW propane. Coal-tar heat uses the complete heavy-fuel-oil furnace on which the source explicitly based its proxy, with fuel sourcing, composition, PAH/metals, allocation and emissions differences. Two straw and six pulp-mill heat entries use complete native biomass heat screening proxies; industrial wood replaces straw, and wood-chip CHP replaces pulp-mill/black-liquor recovered heat. Cultivation/organic status, ash/alkali, chemical recovery, feedstock, source coproduct versus native exergy allocation, scale and emissions differences are explicit; no source internal inventory or LCIA equivalence is asserted. For 48 gas-plant heat outputs and one coke furnace, source allocated fuel demand per heat MJ drives native per-fuel-MJ combustion; do not equate fuel MJ to heat MJ. Native blast-furnace gas excludes fuel production whereas source buys gas: retain this upstream boundary/allocation difference explicitly; native coke-oven fuel production stays included. For refinery heat, preserve audited gas mass by source kg divided by native kg per fuel MJ, retaining source reference ambiguity and native infrastructure difference without inferred thermal efficiency. For 24 bagasse/oil CHP outputs and one EAF heat output, source nonproduction coordinates are proportional to companion electricity/steel inventory; the audited ratio weights the complete native donor as an allocated-burden proxy, not physical electricity consumption or a steel purchase. Native bagasse donor includes economic agricultural/refinery/distillery allocation; source separate combustion allocation differs. Native oil fleet/CHP share, EAF steel/slag allocation, output heat quality and internal uncertainties differ. These ratios do not establish native allocation equivalence or an energy-unit conversion. Twelve exact positive source heat outputs contain production only; use the verified native positive recovered-heat output whose documented allocation is 100% to waste disposal and 0% to energy and whose inventory likewise contains production only. Retain their original heat shares with explicit waste/feedstock/technology/geography proxy warnings, not an invented zero physical combustion or empty disposal service. Six municipal recovered-heat wrappers use that same complete native recovered-heat service at plant gate; source internal regional routing, recovery and allocation are replaced, not claimed identical. No generic empty-provider fallback, zero-burden helper or omission authorization is introduced. Source producer internal formulas, parameters, exchanges and uncertainty are replaced by the specified native models; audited driver coefficients and market/caller quantities remain distinct. Native bundle pin and 2,991 upstream biosphere exclusions persist. All proxy score effects remain unquantified. Preserve caller ownership, formulas, signed uncertainty, foreground links and separate exchanges. Uninspected profiles, standalone producers, reverse or cross-system-model routes and full scenario/certification/export are outside this decision.

limitations: One positive kg of hard-coal-ash treatment service reconstructed from the original negative-one-kg market. Retain every nonempty receiving-process quantity and each freight row in source order; convert the negative waste-reference demands to positive disposal-service inputs with factor -1 and consistent uncertainty scaling. Omit only independently proven production-only zero-price cut-off receivers, retaining every source identity, signed quantity, statistics and inventory hash in the review omission audit. Do not renormalize the remaining disposal shares or add recovery credits. Preserve the source residual-landfill/sanitary-landfill/incineration split. Native Swiss municipal incineration lacks the source Swiss fly-ash extraction; warn about extraction, residue recovery, allocation and emissions differences, without adding a recovery credit. Native regional landfill processes and reviewed rail/fleet proxies carry geography, technology, vintage and internal-uncertainty limitations. Original positive freight quantities remain positive; negative-reference normalization is not a blanket sign flip of transport.

Only the individually inspected ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off identities qualify. Native utilities, coal grades, delivery, transport fleets, geography, technology, allocation, vintage, internal uncertainty and biosphere coverage are screening approximations with unquantified score effects. Preserve original production/reactivation shares, all nonempty process inputs, signed caller quantities, uncertainty, formulas, direct emissions and freight; no renormalization or recovered-material/energy credit. Exactly 51 proven empty negative-reference cut-off ash receivers are omitted from the two ash helper inventories with identity/quantity/hash audits; no nonempty receiving inventory is omitted. Source emptiness does not authorize zero-burden substitutes elsewhere. Other versions and consequential conversions are not newly approved.

operations.authorization: Active all-sector shared-Premise goal and standing auto-approval for independently inspected native proxies/reconstructions and scoped omissions with warnings and recorded decisions. Ash allocation review recorded in Premise 82b64f51. No nonempty inventory omission.

limitations: One positive kg of virgin granular activated carbon from hard coal. Preserve original delivered-coal feedstock quantities, every regional electricity and heat input, infrastructure, water, 72 direct biosphere exchanges and local parameters. Do not substitute carbon black, carbon fibre or mercury-bearing waste disposal. Preserve kg of hard-coal feedstock using complete native delivered regional-storage supply, not mine-only coal or an energy-normalized coal-combustion service. Original country input rows and source coal quantities remain separate. ID uses AU, CN uses CPA, RNA uses US, and RoW uses the complete UCTE storage mix as explicit geographic/feedstock proxies. Grade, carbon/ash/moisture content, mining, allocation, delivery, vintage and internal uncertainty differ; no LHV, carbon-content, moisture or yield multiplier is established. Retain separately modeled source combustion emissions without adding another combustion stage. Preserve each negative ash demand as a positive reviewed treatment-service demand using factor -1. Six biosphere labels per inventory are canonical publisher renames with unchanged UUID, compartment and unit, not substance or ionic-mass proxies. No original emission, nonempty input or parameter is omitted, aggregated, renormalized or replaced by a theoretical carbon/water balance. Native utility/geography/technology differences and original inventory limitations remain explicit.

limitations: One positive kg of reactivated granular carbon, despite the source treatment name; do not flip the product reference. Preserve its actual reactivation energy, infrastructure, water, 72 direct biosphere exchanges, parameters and positive spent-carbon stock demand. The existing reviewed spent-carbon market retains its positive-reference cut-off stock allocation and complete freight; that stock is not mercury-waste disposal and does not make reactivation burden-free. Preserve kg of hard-coal feedstock using complete native delivered regional-storage supply, not mine-only coal or an energy-normalized coal-combustion service. Original country input rows and source coal quantities remain separate. ID uses AU, CN uses CPA, RNA uses US, and RoW uses the complete UCTE storage mix as explicit geographic/feedstock proxies. Grade, carbon/ash/moisture content, mining, allocation, delivery, vintage and internal uncertainty differ; no LHV, carbon-content, moisture or yield multiplier is established. Retain separately modeled source combustion emissions without adding another combustion stage. Preserve each negative ash demand as a positive reviewed treatment-service demand using factor -1. Six biosphere labels per inventory are canonical publisher renames with unchanged UUID, compartment and unit, not substance or ionic-mass proxies. No original emission, nonempty input or parameter is omitted, aggregated, renormalized or replaced by a theoretical carbon/water balance. Native utility/geography/technology differences and original inventory limitations remain explicit.

Only the individually inspected ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off identities qualify. Native utilities, coal grades, delivery, transport fleets, geography, technology, allocation, vintage, internal uncertainty and biosphere coverage are screening approximations with unquantified score effects. Preserve original production/reactivation shares, all nonempty process inputs, signed caller quantities, uncertainty, formulas, direct emissions and freight; no renormalization or recovered-material/energy credit. Exactly 51 proven empty negative-reference cut-off ash receivers are omitted from the two ash helper inventories with identity/quantity/hash audits; no nonempty receiving inventory is omitted. Source emptiness does not authorize zero-burden substitutes elsewhere. Other versions and consequential conversions are not newly approved.

The existing reviewed spent-carbon market retains its positive-reference cut-off stock allocation and complete freight; that stock is not mercury-waste disposal and does not make reactivation burden-free. Preserve kg of hard-coal feedstock using complete native delivered regional-storage supply, not mine-only coal or an energy-normalized coal-combustion service. Original country input rows and source coal quantities remain separate. ID uses AU, CN uses CPA, RNA uses US, and RoW uses the complete UCTE storage mix as explicit geographic/feedstock proxies. Grade, carbon/ash/moisture content, mining, allocation, delivery, vintage and internal uncertainty differ; no LHV, carbon-content, moisture or yield multiplier is established. Retain separately modeled source combustion emissions without adding another combustion stage. Preserve each negative ash demand as a positive reviewed treatment-service demand using factor -1. Six biosphere labels per inventory are canonical publisher renames with unchanged UUID, compartment and unit, not substance or ionic-mass proxies. No original emission, nonempty input or parameter is omitted, aggregated, renormalized or replaced by a theoretical carbon/water balance. Native utility/geography/technology differences and original inventory limitations remain explicit.

Only the individually inspected ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off identities qualify. Native utilities, coal grades, delivery, transport fleets, geography, technology, allocation, vintage, internal uncertainty and biosphere coverage are screening approximations with unquantified score effects. Preserve original production/reactivation shares, all nonempty process inputs, signed caller quantities, uncertainty, formulas, direct emissions and freight; no renormalization or recovered-material/energy credit. Exactly 51 proven empty negative-reference cut-off ash receivers are omitted from the two ash helper inventories with identity/quantity/hash audits; no nonempty receiving inventory is omitted. Source emptiness does not authorize zero-burden substitutes elsewhere. Other versions and consequential conversions are not newly approved.

Native European rail and generic lorry fleets are geographic/technology screening proxies at original tonne-km. This is not proof of real compost being impact-free; score differences from freight, biosphere conventions and source boundaries remain unquantified. No other profile, waste-treatment reference or nonzero stock is approved.

Retain the global market material shares and all four freight rows, the original RER/RoW lime split, every RER lime producer/freight entry and the previously reviewed RoW lime delivery helper without renormalization. Use complete native milled limestone, the matching native algal-lime regional-storage process and the separately reviewed allocated zinc-mining co-product burden, with quarry, energy, infrastructure, ore, allocation, geography, vintage and internal-uncertainty limitations. All three recovered sludge-derived pH products have positive one-kg references and 75 nominal-zero deterministic biosphere rows in total; paired negative-one-kg waste-treatment branches are nonempty. CA-QC/RoW retain 50 background formulas identical to the waste branch. Read-only evaluation reproduces all 50 nonzero waste values, including four expressions requiring one case-only alias clarification; those expressions do not describe the zero-allocated recovered product. Preserve the observed fixed-profile product allocation with an explicit empty recovered-stock handover. Do not transplant unallocated treatment formulas as recovered-product emissions. Background parameter recalculation equivalence is not claimed. This does not clear waste treatment or separately listed caller field emissions and does not omit caller formulas. No real landfarming process is asserted impact-free, and no recovery/soil-carbon credit is added. The source RER algal branch and native algal process both document marine collection, drying from 25% to 2.5% water and milling; preserve its original kg share with the complete native inventory once, no drying or moisture multiplier. Its FR-production/CH-delivery label, infrastructure, allocation, upstream supply, internal uncertainty and vintage differ. Native European rail, generic road, barge and oceanic container freight replace source fleets at original tonne-km, with geographic/technology warnings and unquantified score differences. Other profiles, waste references, or changed source allocations require independent review.

limitations: Exact requested 3.7 cut-off only, using explicitly limited 3.7.1 functional-reference and fixed-allocation proxy evidence. Keep two separate native treatment shares 0.397600148816246 and 0.397566014085865, original road 0.01932 and rail 0.0112 tonne-km and their marginal uncertainty. Do not renormalise to one kg of incineration, divide by dry matter or add fuel/energy/recovery credits. The remaining 0.204833837097889 kg is a clinker-kiln waste receipt with 57 zero allocated nominal exchanges and zero uncertainty bounds; all inherited formulas also occur in the nonzero clinker activity. Explicitly omit that allocated-zero receipt from the target supplier graph and retain its signed quantity and evidence in the omission audit. This is not a claim that physical co-processing or kiln emissions are zero; parameter recalculation and other allocations are not represented. Source negative waste reference becomes positive target treatment reference at factor -1; keep internal treatment/transport burdens positive. Geography, vintage, technology, uncertainty, fleet and native biosphere exclusions differ and score effects are unquantified.

Source quantities, allocation and omission are adopted as screening assumptions. Omission hash and original index identify the inspected patch proxy witness only, not a directly inspected bare-3.7 vector; no cross-version inventory or score equality is asserted.

limitations: Only the exact inspected ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off RER 16-32t Euro V freight market is reviewed. Source market contains one positive unit share of its full RER service. Use only the nine available native RER Euro-V diesel services: 18t, 26t and 32t rated gross weight crossed with long haul, regional delivery and urban delivery. Each complete service has a positive one-tkm reference in native2025 and native2026. Their size/duty weights are the existing native 16-32t fleet coefficients conditional on Euro V and normalized within that subset. The inspected 2025/2026 nominal subset and coefficients are identical. This normalizes native proxy evidence, not the source inventory or caller tkm; no Euro III/IV/VI or electric/hybrid supply is included.

The Swiss2020 native conditional size/duty distribution is a screening proxy because the source supplies only an average 16-32t Euro V service and does not resolve these weights. Native RER labels retain Swiss model/fleet provenance; original German/European HBEFA3.1 source emissions, payloads, routes, SCR/EGR mixture, upstream fuel, infrastructure, vintage and internal uncertainty can differ. Technology-year2010 labels identify the available native Euro-V models, not an IAM fleet forecast. Source/native numerical LCI, LCIA and stochastic equivalence and quantified score effects are not established.

Retain complete native suppliers once and the original source one-tkm demand. Add no source operating emissions, fuel, truck, road, maintenance or end-of-life burden on top; do not scale by gross vehicle weight, payload, distance, fuel consumption, EURO-class emission ratio, capacity or lifetime. The previous unconditioned all-standards fleet-average draft is superseded and has no active source-3.9 Premise grant.

limitations: Only the independently inspected ecoinvent 3.9 cut-off Swiss waste-PVF market and fly-ash-extraction treatment profiles are reviewed. Source production references are negative one kg of waste; native disposal is positive one kg of service. Factor -1 converts negative waste inputs into positive treatment demand, preserving supported caller uncertainty, formulas and separate emissions. Do not clamp exchange signs or confuse PVF disposal with polymer production.

The complete native Swiss PVF incinerator is a screening proxy: the same 0.2% water, upper/lower heating values 28.09/27.89 MJ per kg and documented net energy 3.53 MJ electricity and 6.9 MJ heat. Retain the complete native treatment once; no energy, combustion, infrastructure or ash treatment is added a second time.

The source includes fly-ash extraction and 0.00915 kg dry hydroxide sludge recovered for zinc furnaces per kg waste. Native ordinary incineration lacks that recovery and has different residue/solidification inventories: source bottom ash/residues/cement 0.308/0.1782/0.07127 kg versus native slag/residues/cement 0.3223/0.3313/0.1325 kg. Source/native carbon composition also differs slightly. Preserve warnings for missing ash extraction and recovery, changed disposal burdens, emissions, allocation, vintage, native biosphere exclusions, internal uncertainty and unquantified score differences. Do not invent a recovery credit, separate source residue stages or an efficiency multiplier.

The market retains original collection: 0.00356 tkm rail and 0.02577 tkm generic lorry per kg treated, including supported uncertainty. These positive inputs remain positive after normalizing the market to a positive treatment-service reference; the original negative waste-treatment input becomes positive native treatment. Complete RER rail and lorry fleet are explicit geography/fleet proxies for Swiss collection. No collection loss, payload, fuel or route correction is introduced. Other source releases, system models and reverse routes remain unapproved.
